# Kyoto 3-Day Trip Plan for 2 Adults

A moderate-paced Kyoto itinerary for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-12** with **temples, food markets, and one relaxed nature activity**. I’ve kept it to **no more than 2 major sights per day** and targeted the full trip to stay within **JPY 120,000 excluding flights**.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1 — Higashiyama temples + classic Kyoto food
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Kiyomizu-dera, then a slow walk through the preserved lanes of Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka.
- **Afternoon:** Lunch around Gion or Higashiyama, then Yasaka Shrine for an easy second major stop.
- **Dinner:** Kyoto-style izakaya or yudofu dinner near Gion.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Replace the walking lanes with Kyoto National Museum or a longer café + sweets stop in Gion.

### Day 2 — Market morning + nature reset
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Nishiki Market for breakfast bites, seasonal snacks, and souvenir food shopping.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning:** Nishiki Market for breakfast bites, seasonal snacks, and souvenir food shopping, Kyoto, Japan
- **Afternoon:** Arashiyama bamboo grove area and a relaxed riverside stroll; keep this as your one nature-focused day.
- **Dinner:** Tofu, soba, or a casual kaiseki-style set meal in western Kyoto.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Swap Arashiyama for Arashiyama Monkey Park only if weather is light; otherwise use Kyoto Railway Museum or a department-store food hall.

### Day 3 — Northern Kyoto temples + final food stop
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Kinkaku-ji for your second major temple highlight.
- **Afternoon:** Ryoan-ji or Daitoku-ji area if you want one more temple stop, or keep it lighter with a tea break and souvenir shopping.
- **Dinner:** Final meal near Kyoto Station or downtown Kawaramachi for easy departure logistics.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Replace the temple pair with Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art, Teramachi shopping arcades, or a tea/craft workshop.

## Cost Plan for 2 Adults

| Category | Estimated Cost | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Accommodation, 2 nights | JPY 30,000–45,000 | Mid-range hotel or ryokan-style stay |
| Local transport | JPY 6,000–10,000 | Subway, buses, occasional taxi |
| Temple admissions | JPY 4,000–8,000 | Depends on exact temple choices |
| Food markets + lunches | JPY 12,000–18,000 | Nishiki, snacks, casual lunches |
| Dinners | JPY 18,000–28,000 | 3 dinners for 2 adults |
| Tea/café breaks | JPY 4,000–8,000 | Matcha, sweets, coffee stops |
| Nature activity | JPY 0–4,000 | Arashiyama stroll is free; optional paid add-on |
| Flex / rainy-day changes | JPY 8,000–12,000 | Museum entry, taxi buffer, extra snacks |
| **Trip total** | **JPY 82,000–133,000** | Aiming for **JPY 110,000–120,000** is realistic with moderate dining |

## Budget-Friendly Trip Shape

- Stay near **Kyoto Station, Gion, or Kawaramachi** for easy movement and fewer taxi costs.
- Use **Nishiki Market + casual lunches** to keep food spending balanced.
- Choose **1 paid temple-heavy day, 1 market/nature day, 1 lighter temple day** to avoid overload.
- If you want to stay comfortably under budget, cap dinners at **JPY 5,000–7,000 per night for two**.
